MutationObserver

The MutationObserver interface provides the ability to watch for changes being made to the DOM tree. It is designed as a replacement for the older Mutation Events feature, which was part of the DOM3 Events specification.

Observers are cheap to create and are only charged for the mutations they observe. An observer that watches a subtree it does not need will be handed records it must then discard.

Constructor

Creates and returns a new observer which invokes a specified callback when DOM events occur. The callback is passed the list of records and the observer itself.

Instance methods

disconnect()
Stops the instance from receiving further notifications until and unless observe is called again.
observe()
Configures the observer to begin receiving notifications through its callback function when DOM changes matching the given options occur.
takeRecords()
Removes all pending notifications from the observer's notification queue and returns them in a new array of records.

Notes

The callback runs after the current task, not synchronously with each change, so a burst of mutations arrives as one list. Records are delivered in the order the changes happened.

Disconnecting inside the callback is allowed and stops further delivery at once. Reconnecting later starts a fresh queue; earlier records are not replayed.

An observer holds no strong reference to the nodes it watches, so watched nodes can still be garbage collected when nothing else keeps them alive.

Related pages for Web APIs: ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver.
